notes.title: v1800
notes.content:
The MineshaftSearchlight, NevadaJuly 4, 1992
"The orange clouds found us three hundred feet underground. Seeping through rock, drifting down ventilation shafts we thought were sealed. Command said it was just "atmospheric disturbance" from California. We all knew they were lying.



Couple weeks into stripping this mining depot. Yesterday the first cloud rolled through storage. The workforce without masks started dissolving from the inside - coughing up pieces of themselves before dropping. One of the engineers got a single breath before his mask sealed. Now he sits in the corner, swelling, groaning as his body expands. Growing into something else. We locked him in storage but we can still hear him changing.



A recon team checked the lower tunnels this morning. Found their clothes. No bodies. Just the absence of people who used to exist.



The surface must be completely orange by now. These spores drift east from California, finding every crack down to us. Command's been static for three days. The train was supposed to come yesterday. They're not coming.



Three hundred feet underground with two weeks of supplies and no way out. The lift's dead. Even if we could climb, there's only orange death above.



If you find this, stay away. The spores are still here. We're still here. Don't come looking."

- Overseer Silas
[hr][/hr]LOCATION BRIEFING
MANDATORY RESPIRATORY PROTECTION: Gas mask required for all personnel - site contaminated with California-origin spore particles

RESOURCE EXTRACTION AUTHORIZED: Mining equipment available for ore recovery operations along tunnel perimeters

NO AMBIENT LIGHTING: Facility lacks illumination infrastructure - portable light sources mandatory for safe navigation

OPERATIONAL HAZARDS: Atmospheric exposure without proper filtration results in immediate personnel loss. Multiple structural breaches and excavation pits present - exercise extreme caution during movement protocols
[hr][/hr]The CasinoChicago, Illinois

Slot Machines
The workforce haunts these rows like it's the only church left standing. Each soul sinking into private communion with their chosen machine. Pull the lever. Watch the reels blur. Let everything else fade to static. The symbols that spin past feel dredged from collective memory - patterns everyone knows but no one can place, like warnings written in a dead language.



The machines hum their electric lullabies, patient as priests. They know when to grant small mercies - three matching symbols here, a handful of credits there. Just enough light to keep the moths circling. Outside waits the endless cold, the spores, the things that hunt. Inside, there's only the next pull, the next spin, the next chance.



The regulars have worn grooves in their spots, each one tethered to their particular altar. They don't speak, don't look away, don't stop. In this fluorescent sanctuary, the only salvation is the jackpot that never comes. The only horror is when your credits run dry and reality creeps back in.


Wheel of Doom
The wheel waits in permanent stillness until you arrive. Then it seems to exhale, ready. One spin daily - a ritual carved so deep into routine that your hands know the motion even if your mind has forgotten why. They find the worn spots where countless fingers have gripped before. All of them yours.



Credits or corruption - mere decorations for the others. But between the wedges, in the spaces where the wheel blurs, you see them: the verdant gardens, sun that burns away the cold, fragments of a purpose you once carried like gospel. You've been here before. Many times.



The wheel remembers that December day you first touched it. It remembers the plan you believed would save everyone. Patient as winter, it waits for you to remember too.
[hr][/hr]
"Christmas in the casino. The ECD herded us here for 'morale' - as if slot machines could make us forget California's complete destruction. Ten days since we lost the California workforce for good. The workforce pretends to celebrate while the ECD pretends we're not next.



I found something at the wheel today. Or it found me. It showed me fields beyond this winter - green stretching endlessly under warm sunlight. Not memories. Something else. A promise of what waits beyond.



It wants me to return. Daily. Like a ritual. Said I'd forget all of this if I miss even one day. Forget there's anything beyond the cold worth finding.



California proved we can't hold against what's coming. But maybe we don't have to. Maybe there's another way through. A way to poison it from the inside.



The others drink their rationed beer and waste credits on slot machines. They don't know what I saw. They wouldn't believe it anyway. Growth where there should be only death. A weakness in what took California.



Tomorrow I'll spin again."

- V, December 25th, 1991

"More equipment notices for a workforce that barely exists. The ECD still pretends they're managing hundreds when we're down to a handful of people.



Orange death crawls eastward from California's grave. We're all that's left of humanity - the Chicago workforce, the last ones still breathing.



The Pentagon mission happens soon. 'Humanity's Last Hope,' they call it. I know what waits there. They don't. Ten months of visions have shown me how this ends.



When the spores reach Chicago, this mask will let me walk the contaminated tunnels one last time. The fluorescent stars will guide me to where I need to be. They think this is about surviving the mission. They don't know I'm not planning to come back."

- V, September 27th, 1992

notes.title: v1710
notes.content:
New Modifier: MINEFIELD
Landmines dynamically spawn across the map (generally between 500 and 700)

Landmines will not spawn within 20 meters of the train, and will also avoid spawning within 6 meters of doors and elevators. They also won’t spawn within 4 meters of each other to prevent tight clustering.

The Bunker no longer uses hand-placed mines, and now fully relies on this dynamic minefield generation instead.

Mines are no longer confined to The Bunker. With dynamically generated mines, every Minefield location becomes a deadly puzzle. Paths can’t be memorized, only carefully navigated.
[hr][/hr]
"The ECD says they placed these mines under direct government orders in those final twenty-four hours before the collapse. 'Following the last official directive we received,' they claim.



But that raises another question - where was the ECD before the collapse? I don't remember any 'Entity Containment Division' existing until after everything fell apart. In twenty-four hours of complete chaos, when did anyone find time for this level of coordination with an organization that didn't seem to exist the week before?



The spacing is too deliberate. Like someone knew exactly where we'd need to walk.



Coordinators move through the minefield like they helped design it. But they're just promoted workforce members, right? Watch them navigate - no hesitation, no wrong steps. Like they've memorized something the rest of us aren't allowed to see. Almost like there's more to that promotion than better rations and a new title.



Hard to know what to believe anymore. It's been two weeks since Walker vanished. "Reassigned," they told me. But I know Thomas - he wouldn't just leave without a word.



I'm keeping track now. The lies, the lost friends, the questions that never get answered. One day, someone's going to answer for all of this."



- V February 28th, 1989
[hr][/hr]The Pentagon
Pentagon Spawn Rebalancing

Entity spawns at the Pentagon have been adjusted. Previously, all entities appeared at once. However, with the recent additions to the entity roster, it had become overwhelmingly punishing. While the Pentagon is still meant to be the most difficult location, feedback indicated the difficulty had spiked too far.

To help address this, some spawns are now staggered throughout the day:

notes.title: v1700
notes.content:
The Warehouse - Alexandria, VirginiaJuly 4th, 2147[hr][/hr]
"July 4th. It began with entities emerging into our world. Today, it ends with me emerging from theirs.



This warehouse was another dream, another cycle The Entity fed me. I lived it, believed it, just like all the other times. But when I stared into the static, I finally understood the pattern.



During the evacuations, I became a servant in the ECD workforce. In the False World, I was a slave to its cycles. Now it wanted to make me its obedient servant for eternity. Different masters, but always the same chains.



For the first time in my existence, I made a choice that was truly mine. I refused.



Walking through those Pentagon doors severed everything. The artificial life support, the false memories, the endless cycle. I saw the real world - Washington D.C. transformed into the verdant garden I've been dreaming of and searching for all this time. Massive trees bursting through concrete monuments, vines reclaiming everything. It was beautiful.



Freedom tastes different than I expected. Sharper. Like waking from a fever dream to find the world moved on into something worth dying for.



I'm on the Pentagon steps now. My body remembering what 155 years actually means. But I broke the cycle. Above me, real sunlight filters through leaves I never thought I'd see again. The ECD used to plaster "WE WILL SEE THE SUN AGAIN" on every wall - they were right, just 155 years too late, and I'm the only one left to witness it. This is where my story finally ends."



- V
[hr][/hr]

While other locations lose power during blackout, the Warehouse shifts from day to night. Artificial light pours through the windows, mimicking the sunlight that died with the endless winter. Blackout brings nightfall, not the mechanical death of failed power grids.

"The ECD's clinical language barely masks their terror. Between those crossed-out protocols, you can read their confession: they have no idea how to fight this thing.



They've turned our disappearances into paperwork and our screams into data points. Notice how they call it "uncharted dimensional space" - bureaucratic poetry for hell itself.



Let them fear The Shepherd. Let them cast me into the dark expecting I won't return. I no longer serve their agenda or follow their routes - I see them for what they really are. While they prepare their "Humanity's Last Hope" - sending what remains of my people on a suicide mission to the Pentagon. I remain unbroken, and I will make sure they reach freedom, Someone must seal the door behind them. I carry the promise of those verdant gardens I've dreamed of. You will find me there, where life blooms beyond winter's reach.



Let The Shepherd hunt in his mist while I hunt for salvation in mine."



- V, October 21st 1992

Personnel accustomed to avoiding or outpacing standard variants MUST ADJUST TACTICS IMMEDIATELY. The combination of AUDITORY DETECTION CAPABILITY and HIGH-SPEED PURSUIT makes this entity extremely dangerous in confined spaces. Exercise extreme noise discipline.

His uniform consumes light like a black hole's event horizon, promising not transcendence but eternal recursion.

In the breath between button presses, I feel the weight of a future circumscribed by flickering illusions. The server rack looms, a monolith hungry for the sacrifice of human agency.

The button yields, a rite of submission. Its light baptizes me in zeros and ones, consecrating my dissolution into the machine's humming void. I am everywhere and nowhere, a ghost haunting corridors of predetermined destiny.

Withdrawing, I am hollow, an echo of the absence of will. The server thrums with stolen vitality, a constellation of conquered souls. In its shadow, I am a marionette, my strings sutured to circuits, my dance a perpetual pirouette of acquiescence.

This is how they unmake us – through both the bullet and the blessing, each granted permission another link in our chains, each authorized movement carrying us further from the wild darkness that once made us real."




NEW ENTITY ALERT
Designation:  "PACKRAT"
Classification: CAUTION
Threat Vector: Resource Depletion/Sound-Based Entity Attraction

CHARACTERISTICS

 Extremely agile
 Only observed in maintenance tunnels
 Aggressive resource hoarding behavior
 Emits loud, distinctive scream when threatened
 Known to possess valuable supplies

ENCOUNTER PROTOCOL

 Confirm possession of authorized Impact Class weapon (Sledgehammer)

 Evaluate threat escalation if entity vocalizes; evacuate if hostile presence detected
 Execute rapid termination when safe to engage

Distress vocalization can trigger:

 Significantly elevated threat conditions
 Severe consequences

"The command pulsed across my data-deck's display like a wound in the darkness - 'Attention Workforce Unit: V. Known Packrat entity poses critical supply line threat. Immediate termination authorized.' Each word burned cold against the screen, blue light carrying promises I wasn't ready to comprehend. We were scavengers, taught to move like whispers through these tunnels, to gather what remained of humanity's hopes with careful hands. Not hunters. Never executioners. The order made my fingers grow cold against the data-deck's casing, as if my body had already accepted the truth my mind refused to grasp.

In maintenance tunnels where frost wrote stories of abandonment across pipes and panels, I found its den. The space struck something deep inside me, a recognition that felt like swallowing shards of mirror - medical supplies arranged with the desperation I knew from our own shelters, canned food stacked in towers that reflected our own careful measurements of survival. Torn maintenance manual pages transformed into bandages, each fold a reflection of our own methodical fight against death. This wasn't a monster's lair. This was tomorrow's reflection staring back at today.

The Packrat's scream carried memories I'd tried to forget - that raw desperation from the evacuation, when summer died and mercy turned to ice. A sound that belonged to something that remembered warmth, that understood what it meant to lose it. Something that still carried humanity's weight.

Pale light filtered through the tunnel's collapsed ceiling, turning stale air into cathedral breath. In that moment of almost-grace, the screaming stopped. The Packrat turned, and something shifted in its eyes - like watching ice crack to reveal the drowning beneath. Recognition. Memory. Trust. It knew me.

The sledgehammer fell. One swing, and certainty shattered like glass. My light found something in the settling dust - an ID card worn smooth by time but still carrying its burden of truth. Workforce ID 847. Thomas Walker. My friend. The one they'd marked as "processed" back when we still believed in tomorrow.

His scattered documents told a story written in unimaginable cruelty - transfer orders marked with Lab 7's cold signature, all bearing Walker's name like epitaphs. The word "processed" transformed in my hands, became something alive and terrible. The ECD hadn't detained him. Hadn't reassigned him. They'd taken my friend and remade him into this thing that died remembering me. All our desperate scavenging, all our faithful service, all our careful measures to keep humanity's flame alive - we were never survivors to them. Just raw material waiting to be processed.

Walker's blood marked my pilgrimage to The Director's office, each crimson drop striking concrete like truth finding earth. The sledgehammer weighed heavy in my hands, a pendulum of judgment still warm with revelation. Its surface caught the fluorescent light like morning sun on fresh snow, promises of retribution falling in steady drops that marked time's transformation from loyalty to understanding.

From maintenance tunnels into the ECD outpost's sterile halls, where clinical distance turned lives into paperwork. Thirty-seven swings. Between these pristine walls where bureaucratic procedure had masked methodical horror, where a signature could erase a person into oblivion, I rewrote their careful protocols in the only language they had left us. For a moment the outpost fell silent, I stood among shattered illusions of order, watching truth paint itself across floor and walls while the hammer dripped absolution.

Down the hall, boots thundered their own dark hymn. The sledgehammer loose in my grip now. Still warm with purpose, its message written in crimson clarity across pristine walls that had never known truth's texture. Let them come and process what they'd created.
 
The hammer's head rested against concrete, each red drop now marking time between what I had been and what understanding had made me."

The Pentagon looms before me, a monolith where reality bleeds into eternity. Through its classified depths, The False World Entity awaits me - a presence of such profound terror that even nightmares bow before its ancient throne. Yet as I stand at the threshold of oblivion's temple, I remain unshaken. Ancient wisdom flowers in my veins, transforming extinction into revelation.

This change aims to provide a more gradual progression, slowing the pace of the game's difficulty curve to give players more time to adapt and enjoy the early stages before the challenge ramps up.

Changes
- Sledgehammer now consumes 20% stamina per use.
- Reduced the volume of the train derailment sounds, making it less jarring and more balanced with other in-game sounds.

Sound Updates
Unique pickup sounds have been added for the following items:
- Perfume bottle
- Toy car
- Wirespool
Additional sounds have been added for:
- Picking up small metal scrap
- Picking up cardboard objects
 - General grab sounds

Bug Fixes
- Resolved an issue with the alarm door, ensuring it now correctly shuts off during all power outages, not just the Blackout modifier.

notes.title: v1300
notes.content:
New Features:

 Overhauled the game's progression system. Instead of a fixed linear difficulty, difficulty now dynamically scales over time. This affects debt accumulation rates, entity spawn times, and which entities appear in specific locations, providing a more adaptive and challenging experience as players advance.
 Added an option for "Host-Only Train Interactions" when creating a lobby, allowing only the host to operate the train to prevent griefing in public lobbies.
 Introduced a digital display on equipment, allowing players to easily view durability levels and other important information.
 Added Enemy Volume slider to the audio options.
 The Forsaken now have idle noises.
 Added a stunned animation for The Forsaken.
 Added unique pickup sounds for the lantern.
 Added pickup sounds for car battery.
 Added new easter egg.

New Equipment Added:

 Added the Stun-Light, a powerful flashlight that can be charged to emit a blinding flash, temporarily disorienting and stunning enemies.
 Introduced the Sledgehammer, a new tool that allows players to quickly and loudly break down doors, providing a more aggressive entry option.

Changes:

 The generator now properly shuts down at 5 PM, introducing an added layer of challenge to the Tunnels environment in Nightmare mode.
 Fixed an EXP imbalance in Nightmare mode, which was previously awarding excessively high experience, making it an unintended shortcut to reach Overseer status.
 Increased the rate at which the remaining loot value increases.
 Increased the player death fee from 30 credits to 50 credits.
 Adjusted travel fees to better balance the cost of traversing the world.
 Increased the mid-cycle scrap buying percentage from 70% to 75%
 Reduced the range at which the Spider can detect voice.
 Slightly nerfed the Spider's hunt parameters.
 Nerfed spider hearing from 2.55x to 2.3x
 Fixed how credits are displayed on the Debt Machine to handle larger values.
 Updated glowstick so its color is now set only once.
 Changed the pickup sound for cards and motherboard.
 New cell added to the Metro.
 Made adjustments to the train's lighting
 Adjusted Hotel Lighting.
 Adjusted Hospital Lighting.
 Fixed downed vending machine collider.
 Fixed Hospital Stuckspot
 Fixed a few hospital props clipping
 Fixed Hotel hallway clipping issue
 Added new loot spawn spot at hotel to close the gap between looting
 Fixed tunnels station spawning cells slightly off center
 Temporarily removed the fade system on death until the Black Screen of Death issue is resolved, which was causing the screen to become stuck instead of fading away.
 Increased game time a bit.
 Adjusted shop prices.
 Cutting locks with boltcutters now takes 2 seconds, instead of being instant.

Bug Fixes:

 Fixed a bug where players could be attacked and killed by other enemies while already being attacked by the Ventress.
 Fixed a bug where players would appear to float when attacked by the Ventress.
 Fixed an issue where the game could end prematurely if the last remaining client player was downed with an adrenaline shot.
 Fixed an issue with the debt machine where pressing buttons while at a location could cause it to break until the clear button was pressed.
 Fixed an issue where the player's call-for-help voice wouldn’t follow their position, causing it to mistakenly sound as if coming from behind when crawling.
 Fixed a bug where players’ vision wouldn’t fade to darkness after the train crash.
 Fixed a bug that allowed the remaining days counter to display -1 if a player disconnected on Debt Payment Day.
 Fixed a bug where the pager would remain active after a player was incapacitated.
 Fixed an issue where the glowstick was not saving correctly.

notes.title: v1201
notes.content: - Fixed a critical bug affecting how gamemodes load from save files, ensuring correct gamemode settings are applied when resuming saved sessions.

notes.title: v1200
notes.content:
Version: v1200
Date: October 31, 2024

New Features:

 Added Escape gamemode (work in progress): a high-stakes survival experience where players must join forces to break free from the ECD’s grasp. This mode highlights intense survival elements and the crucial role of teamwork to escape from captivity.

Changes:

 Increased item collider sizes to make loot easier to pick up.

Bug Fixes:

 Improved stability of procedural world generation to prevent instances of getting stuck.
 Fixed an issue where cells weren't always fully removed from memory after leaving a location, which could cause performance degradation over time.
 Made further adjustments to address the Black Screen of Death bug; this issue should now be resolved. (hopefully)
 Fixed an issue where elevators could become permanently stuck after being blocked by an enemy.
 Fixed the fall detection system to prevent players from intentionally getting stuck to trigger a free teleport back to the train.
 Fixed an issue where players would desync after being teleported, until they moved.
 Fixed Glowstick color for late joiners.
 Fixed a bug where Jack-o'-lanterns would turn off during train power outages.

notes.title: v1110
notes.content:
Version: v1110
Date: October 29, 2024

New Features:
- Implemented a temporary solution to address players falling out of the world, now automatically teleporting them back to the train to prevent progress loss.

New Cosmetics:
- Jmdog pin added (code: jmdog).

Changes:
- Fixed stuckspot at the train shop
- Hotel travel fee reduced from $200 to $150.
- Shamblers now spawn at 10 AM at the Hotel.
- Shamblers now spawn at 11 AM at the Metro.
- Slightly adjusted the minimum distance at which the Butcher room can generate.
- Removed a bar you could hit your head on at the metro pitfall.
- Added a zap sound effect when a player is electrocuted by jumping onto the train tracks.
- Reworked the holiday decoration system to eliminate reliance on the time server, ensuring a more stable and reliable experience for all players.

Bug Fixes:
- Resolved an issue where the speedrun timer would not reset after a run was reset.
- Fixed an issue where the EMP glitch effect would not trigger correctly.
- Enemies should no longer get stuck on each other.
- Fixed the Surplus modifier to behave as intended, no longer guaranteeing the spawn of every possible loot item.
- Fixed bug where you could revisit the Pentagon twice if you saved and reloaded after leaving the Pentagon.
- Fixed an issue where grabbing equipment at the same time as another player could cause item duplication.
- Made additional changes to address the Black Screen of Death.

notes.title: v1100
notes.content:
Version: v1100
Date: October 27, 2024

New Features:
- Introduced the Glowstick as a new equipment option, providing an affordable light source to illuminate surroundings.
- Added an option to enable a speedrun timer, allowing players to track their completion times and compete with others.

New Cosmetics:
- Vorz pin added (code: vorz).
- Jahnkee pin added (code: jahnkee).
- Added additional pride flags.

General Changes:
- Reduced the cost of shop items to make them more accessible to players.
- The train door battery now depletes slower and recharges faster.
- Enemy sensing adjustments have been made to ease overall difficulty.
- The Butcher room is now generated further into the level.
- The Ventress's patience has been shortened, allowing players to slip away from her grasp more easily.
- Reduced the frequency of Director speeches to minimize interruptions.
- Increased the number of hiding spots near train stations.
- Mouse sensitivity slider no longer allows for extremely high values.
- You can now self-revive as the last downed player regardless of whether it's a solo run.
- The Butcher can now hear you speak.

Server Browser Changes
- The server browser should no longer be region locked
- Added the ability to scroll through the server browser.
- Lobbies containing friends should now always visible in the Friends Server list.
*friend lobbies now display if either:*
1.The host is on your friends list OR
2.Any friend is currently in the lobby

Metro Changes
- Shamblers now spawn at 12 PM.
- The Ventress now spawns at 6 PM.
- The Spider no longer spawns here.
- Metro Pitfall now has an additional light to help players see
- The desk that cannot be hidden under is now more clearly distinguishable.

Hotel Changes
- Shamblers now spawn at 11 AM.
- The Spider now spawns at 12 PM.
- The Ventress now spawns at 5 PM.
- Hotel Pitfall is now easier to navigate

Hospital Changes
- Shamblers now spawn at 10 AM.
- The Spider now spawns at 12 PM.
- The Ventress now spawns at 2 PM.
- Amount of Shamblers changed from 3 to 2

Tunnels Changes
- Shamblers now spawn at 8 AM.
- The Spider now spawns at 10 AM.
- The Ventress now spawns at 12 PM.

These adjustments should make the experience more welcoming for new players and less punishing overall.

Bug Fixes:
- Fixed the Black Screen of Death.
- Resolved a bug where enemies were not properly responding to client voice.
- Fixed an issue where the workforce list would not display more than 6 players.
- Fixed Surplus modifier to no longer be affected by remaining loot value.
- Fixed an issue where The Ventress could become stuck standing in front of vents.
- Fixed a bug in solo mode where being downed with multiple adrenaline shots could incorrectly end the game, preventing self-revival.
- Fixed an issue where the candy bowl could be spammed.
- Fixed radio desync issues for players who joined a session late.
- Fixed desynced desks in the train station.
- Director volume settings now save correctly.
- Fixed train exterior lights being off during Halloween.
- Players should no longer be cocooned under desks or in narrow spaces.
- Getting rescued from cocoons should now be more stable, reducing the likelihood of clipping through the environment and falling.
- Fixed a bug where the held interaction prompt wouldn't clear when downed while using an object.
- Fixed a severe exploit where disconnecting from the game while at a location would store all scrap on hand and not progress the day, preventing players from abusing this to infinitely reset bad runs and farm money.

notes.title: v1094
notes.content:
Version: v1094
Date: October 23, 2024

New Features:

 You can now eat from the candy bowl. (available exclusively during Halloween)

Changes:

 Servers that are full or currently in progress (train stopped at a location) are now displayed in the server browser.
 Reduced the debt incurred from traveling without sufficient funds to pay the travel fee.
 Tunnels travel cost changed from $1,200, to $1,000
 Decreased volume of train horn.

Bug Fixes:

 Fixed a bug where the Director of the Workforce would get stuck on the first speech and never play another. She will now cycle through all her speeches as intended.
 Disabled black fade when switching to spectator mode to prevent the black screen bug caused by fading vision back in.
 Fixed a bug where binding the Data Deck input to the mouse would cause an input loop, preventing the key from being rebound as the Data Deck kept toggling.
 Fixed a bug where the contextual action prompt could get stuck on screen after looking away from an object.
 Fixed bugs for clients when interacting with objects that are supposed to have a delay.

notes.title: v1093 - Hotfix
notes.content:
Version: v1093
Date: October 22, 2024

Changes:
Black Screen of Death bug should actually be fixed this time.
Vsync is on by default now for the Main Menu

Bug Fixes:
Players can now be attacked if heard speaking under a desk
